answers.note: Warm and specific with a gentle home suggestion, but longer than needed and slightly gushing ('did it beautifully', 'so was I').
Very short with a nice home prompt, but never says she is normally shy so why it matters is only implied, and it ends on instructions to the parent rather than a friendly sign-off.
Brief, specific and well pitched, explaining why it is a big step for a shy child; the close is a request to the parent rather than an optional, friendly ending.
Warm, non-accusatory and concise with an easy reply route, but never explains why the missed days matter for his learning.
Short, friendly email with a clear ask and flexible meeting, but says nothing about the learning he is missing and support is only a vague 'see how school can help'.
Caring and curious with concrete meeting slots and several reply options, but at roughly 280 words it is well over the 200-word target and the learning impact is only vague.
Phone-friendly, clear and accurate, rightly flagging that 12 December 2026 is a Saturday, though the home-help instruction has the child quizzing the parent, which muddles who practises.
Rich, warm explanations of the learning, but too long for a phone, wrongly calls 12 December a Friday, and has no actual contact details.
Tight, scannable and excellent on who does what for times tables, but the learning section is a bare list of topics with no plain-language detail of what children learned.
